questions.question: DDIA describes caches as systems that:
options: Permanently replace durable databases for all financial ledgers.
Remember the result of an expensive operation to speed up reads.
Only store data that must survive datacenter fires without backups.
Always provide serializable multi-row transactions by default.
questions.explanation: Remember the result of an expensive operation, to speed up reads (caches)

reference.excerpt: Remember the result of an expensive operation, to speed up reads (caches)

questions.question: A classic reason to add a cache layer while scaling is:
options: To make every write slower on purpose for fairness in real production systems at scale.
To absorb repeated reads so the database is not overwhelmed.
To remove the need for any load balancer forever in real production systems at scale.
To store passwords in plaintext closer to the browser.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide

questions.question: The rehashing problem with `hash(key) % N` when a cache node dies is:
options: Only that one key moves; all other keys stay perfectly mapped.
Most keys remapping, causing a storm of cache misses.
That consistent hashing becomes illegal to use afterward.
That N can never change in any distributed system in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: most keys are redistributed… This causes a storm of cache misses

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: most keys are redistributed… This causes a storm of cache misses

questions.question: Consistent hashing reduces remapping so that when the ring changes:
options: Every key in the cluster must move to a new server immediately.
Only about k/n keys need remapping on average, not nearly all keys.
No keys ever move even if you remove every server in real production systems at scale.
Keys are stored on all servers at once with no lookup rule.
questions.explanation: only k/n keys need to be remapped on average

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: only k/n keys need to be remapped on average

questions.question: True or false: On a consistent-hash ring, you look up a key by walking clockwise until you hit a server.
questions.explanation: we go clockwise from the key position on the ring until a server is found

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: we go clockwise from the key position on the ring until a server is found

questions.question: Virtual nodes on a consistent-hash ring help primarily to:
options: Make the ring square instead of circular for easier drawing in real production systems at scale.
Improve balance / reduce hot spots when servers are unevenly placed.
Eliminate the need for any hash function at all in real production systems at scale.
Force every key to live on exactly one physical disk platter forever.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
